# Before Vibe Coding: Prompt Engineering {#sec-before}

::: {.callout-warning}
## Writing Status
Pre-draft · Owner: TBD. The brief below is the direction set by the teaching team; the owner will research and rewrite it.
:::

## What This Chapter Covers

Vibe coding did not appear suddenly one day. This chapter covers its prehistory: prompt engineering. It traces the process by which, after the appearance of GPT-3 (2020), "what and how to say to the model" became established as a skill; the process by which techniques like few-shot and chain-of-thought were discovered and systematized; and the process by which the title "prompt engineer" emerged and then faded again. The central question of this chapter is which limitations of prompt engineering called forth the next stage, vibe coding.

## Seed Questions

- When and where was the term prompt engineering first used? What was the trajectory of its popularity?
- What problem was each representative technique (few-shot, chain-of-thought, role assignment, etc.) trying to solve?
- Where did the boundary between "the skill of writing a good prompt" and "the skill of building something through iterative conversation with the model" begin to break down?
- Where does Karpathy's discussion of Software 2.0 (2017) fit into this flow?

## Research Pointers

- Anthropic's and OpenAI's official prompt engineering guide documents
